The knots are not gradually loosened but 'cut' (bhidyante / vimuktaḥ) — like a rope cut with a sharp blade. The blade is knowledge. The knots cannot be untied by effort alone — they must be cut by the sharp edge of direct insight. The connection to the two birds: the knots are what keep the 'eating bird' eating. When the knots are cut, the eating bird looks up, sees the watching bird, and recognises its true identity. The eating stops. Sorrow stops. Identity shifts from the limited to the unlimited.

sk: तदेतदृचाभ्युक्तम् क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रिया ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः स्वयं जुह्वत एकर्षिं श्रद्धयन्तः एतद्ब्रह्मविद्यां ह वै ब्रह्मनिष्ठोऽथ विद्वानुपसन्नं यथाविधिं पुरुषं वेदयेत ||
ro: tat · etat · ṛcā · abhyuktam · kriyāvantaḥ · śrotriyāḥ · brahma-niṣṭhāḥ · svayaṁ · juhvataḥ · eka-ṛṣiṁ · śraddhayantaḥ · etat · brahma-vidyāṁ · ha · vai · brahma-niṣṭhaḥ · atha · vidvān · upasannaṁ · yathā-vidhiṁ · puruṣaṁ · vedayet ||
hi: वह यह ऋचा (Vedic verse) से अभ्युक्त (declared / कहा गया) है — क्रियावन्तः (those engaged in action / कर्मनिष्ठ), श्रोत्रियाः (learned in the Vedas / श्रुति-विद्), ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः (devoted to Brahman / ब्रह्मपरायण) — जो स्वयं जुह्वतः (offering oblations to the one Seer / एक ऋषि को आहुति देते हैं) श्रद्धा से (with faith / श्रद्धापूर्वक) — इस ब्रह्मविद्या (brahma-vidyā / knowledge of Brahman) को वह ब्रह्मनिष्ठ (Brahman-devoted), विद्वान् (wise one) — उपसन्नम् (one who has duly approached / विधिपूर्वक उपसन्न) पुरुष को यथाविधि (according to rule / विधि-अनुसार) वेदयेत् (should teach / बताए)।
en: This is declared (abhyuktam) by the Vedic verse (ṛcā): those who are active (kriyāvantaḥ), learned in the Vedas (śrotriyāḥ), devoted to Brahman (brahma-niṣṭhāḥ), who themselves offer oblations (svayaṁ juhvataḥ) to the one Seer (eka-ṛṣim) with faith (śraddhayantaḥ) — to them should this brahma-vidyā [be taught]. Indeed, the wise one (vidvān), devoted to Brahman (brahma-niṣṭhaḥ), should teach (vedayet) the Person (puruṣam) to one who has duly approached (upasannam) according to rule (yathā-vidhim).

ws.e: learned in the Vedas — from śruti (what is heard = Veda); those who have studied the Vedas under a proper teacher; the prerequisite of Vedic learning
devoted to/established in Brahman — brahma + niṣṭha (established in); not just learned but living in Brahman; cf. 1.2.12: 'śrotriyaṁ brahma-niṣṭham' — the guru must be both learned AND established
the one Seer — eka (one) + ṛṣi (seer); Brahman as the one Seer who sees through all seers; the ultimate object of the inner offering

ws.h: विधिपूर्वक उपसन्न / one who has duly approached
ws.e: one who has properly approached — upa + √sad (to approach/sit near); the student who has come to the teacher with humility and readiness; cf. 1.2.12: 'samit-pāṇi' (fuel in hand)
according to rule / properly — yathā (as) + vidhi (rule/injunction); the teaching must follow proper procedure — the guru-śiṣya paramparā (teacher-student lineage)

gr: The closing instruction: who teaches, who learns: this final mantra of the Khanda describes the transmission protocol for brahma-vidyā — who is qualified to teach it, who is qualified to receive it, and how the transmission should occur. The qualified teacher: (1) kriyāvān — active (not withdrawn from the world), (2) śrotriya — learned in the Vedas (has the intellectual foundation), (3) brahma-niṣṭha — established in Brahman (has direct experience, not just learning). The qualified student: upasanna — one who has 'duly approached' — the student must come with humility, readiness, and sincerity (cf. 1.2.12: samit-pāṇi = 'fuel in hand'). The method: yathā-vidhi — 'according to rule' — the teaching follows the paramparā (lineage of transmission), not arbitrary or casual instruction. The circle closes: the Muṇḍaka began (1.1.1-2) with the lineage of transmission: Brahmā → Atharvā → Aṅgir → Satyavāha → Aṅgiras → Śaunaka. Now it closes by affirming the importance of this lineage — brahma-vidyā is not broadcast indiscriminately but transmitted from qualified teacher to qualified student, according to rule.
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: mundaka_upanishad_3.1.10 — This closing mantra echoes and completes the Muṇḍaka's opening (1.1.1-2) and the guru-instruction of 1.2.12-13. The qualifications for the teacher (kriyāvān, śrotriya, brahma-niṣṭha) match those in 1.2.12: 'tad vijñānārthaṁ sa gurum evābhigacchet samit-pāṇiḥ śrotriyaṁ brahma-niṣṭham' — the guru must be both Veda-learned (śrotriya) AND established in Brahman (brahma-niṣṭha). The addition of 'kriyāvān' (active) here is significant — it echoes 3.1.4 and confirms that the ideal teacher is not withdrawn but engaged. The phrase 'eka-ṛṣim' (the one Seer) is a beautiful epithet for Brahman — Brahman is the single Seer who sees through all eyes, hears through all ears, knows through all minds. The closing formula thus brings the Muṇḍaka full circle — from lineage to lineage, from teacher to teacher.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — ब्रह्मविद्या = केवल अधिकारी (qualified) को ही दी जाए। गुरु = (1) क्रियावान् (active), (2) श्रोत्रिय (Veda-learned), (3) ब्रह्मनिष्ठ (established in Brahman)। शिष्य = उपसन्न (duly approached) — समित्पाणि (1.2.12)। 'यथाविधि' = गुरु-शिष्य परम्परा (teacher-student lineage) का पालन।
advaita.en: Shankara says brahma-vidyā should be given only to the qualified. The guru must be (1) kriyāvān (active), (2) śrotriya (Veda-learned), (3) brahma-niṣṭha (established in Brahman). The student must be upasanna (duly approached) — samit-pāṇi (1.2.12). 'Yathā-vidhi' = following the teacher-student lineage.
advaita.ins: The highest knowledge isn't sold in a market or broadcast on a stage. It flows from qualified teacher to qualified student, through proper channels, according to rule. The teacher must be learned, established, and active. The student must approach with humility and readiness. Then — and only then — the Person is revealed.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — ब्रह्मविद्या = भक्ति-ज्ञान (devotional knowledge) — केवल योग्य शिष्य (qualified student) को — योग्य गुरु (qualified teacher) द्वारा। 'एकर्षिम् जुह्वतः' = एक परमात्मा (one Supreme Lord) को आहुति देने वाले — भगवद्-भक्त (devotees of God)। 'उपसन्नम्' = शरणागत (surrendered) शिष्य।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says brahma-vidyā = devotional knowledge — only to qualified students by qualified teachers. 'Eka-ṛṣim juhvataḥ' = those who offer oblations to the one Supreme Lord — devotees of God. 'Upasannam' = the surrendered student.
vishisht.ins: This knowledge is sacred — not to be given casually. The teacher must be learned, devoted, and active. The student must approach with surrender and faith. Then the teacher reveals the Person — the one Lord who is the Seer behind all seeing, the one reality behind all the rituals, all the knowledge, all the devotion.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — ब्रह्मविद्या = चेतना का ज्ञान (knowledge of consciousness) — व्यक्तिगत संचारण (personal transmission) से। 'एकर्षिम्' = एक चेतना (one consciousness) — जो सब ऋषियों (seers) में देखती है। गुरु-शिष्य सम्बन्ध = चेतना-संचारण (consciousness-transmission) का माध्यम।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says brahma-vidyā = knowledge of consciousness — through personal transmission. 'Eka-ṛṣim' = the one consciousness that sees through all seers. The guru-student relationship = the medium of consciousness-transmission.
aurobindo.ins: This knowledge can't be downloaded — it's transmitted, person to person, consciousness to consciousness. The teacher who is established in Brahman lights the flame in the student who is ready. The one Seer — who looks through every pair of eyes — recognises Itself in both teacher and student. That recognition IS the teaching.

dp.q: 🔍 The guru-śiṣya paramparā — sacred transmission
dp.a: This closing mantra affirms the importance of the guru-śiṣya paramparā (teacher-student lineage) for the transmission of brahma-vidyā: The qualified teacher must be: (1) Kriyāvān (active): not a recluse but engaged with the world — living the knowledge, not just knowing it. (2) Śrotriya (Veda-learned): having studied the Vedas and the Upanishads under a proper teacher — possessing the intellectual framework. (3) Brahma-niṣṭha (established in Brahman): having direct experience of Brahman — not just book-knowledge but living realisation. The qualified student must be: Upasanna (duly approached): having come to the teacher properly — with humility, sincerity, and readiness. The Muṇḍaka's own opening (1.2.12-13) describes this: the student must be 'samit-pāṇi' (with fuel in hand — the traditional mark of readiness), 'praśānta-citta' (with pacified mind), and 'śama-anvita' (possessed of self-control). The method: Yathā-vidhi (according to rule): the teaching follows established procedure — it is not casual, not improvised, not public. It is a sacred act, governed by tradition. The Muṇḍaka's circle: the Upanishad opened with the lineage Brahmā → Atharvā → Aṅgir → Satyavāha → Aṅgiras → Śaunaka. It closes by affirming that this lineage must continue — each generation's Brahman-knower must teach the next generation's qualified student. The chain is unbroken.

dp.q: 🔍 'Eka-ṛṣim' — Brahman as the one Seer
dp.a: The epithet 'eka-ṛṣim' ('the one Seer') is a beautiful and philosophically profound description of Brahman: What it means: Brahman is the one Seer (ṛṣi) who sees through all eyes, thinks through all minds, perceives through all consciousness. Every act of seeing — by every being, in every world — is ultimately an act of the ONE Seer seeing through a particular window. The connection to the two birds: the 'watching bird' (abhicākaśīti) of 3.1.1 is the eka-ṛṣi — the one Seer who watches everything without eating. Every being has this Seer within — it is the witness-consciousness (sākṣin) that underlies all individual awareness. The ritual dimension: 'svayaṁ juhvataḥ eka-ṛṣim' — 'they themselves offer oblations to the one Seer.' This transforms the Vedic ritual: the true oblation is not butter into fire but the offering of oneself (svayam) to the one Seer (Brahman). Every ritual, properly understood, is an offering to the one consciousness that sees through all. The practical implication: in every moment, you are being seen — by the one Seer, the ultimate witness. This isn't surveillance; it's intimacy. The Seer is not judging you — it is YOU, in your deepest nature. The eka-ṛṣi is the second bird on the tree — your own highest Self, watching, always watching, with infinite patience and love.
